resources.string: Local device control service: reads the current screen and performs taps only for apps you allowed. Disable it here or in system settings at any time.

This lets an AI or a local automation app read the current screen and tap, swipe, type and open other apps for you. Only the apps you list below can be touched, and nothing runs until you enable it here and in system accessibility settings. Password fields are never read or tapped. You can revoke everything at any time by switching this off or in system settings.
Not enabled in system accessibility settings.
Enabled in settings but not connected yet. Open the system page and check it.
No app is allowed yet. Add at least one package.
Ready for the apps you allowed.
Off by default. Turning this off immediately stops reads and actions, even if the service is still running.
Capture the accessibility tree of whitelisted apps.
Click, long-press, fill text and gestures inside whitelisted apps.
System-level actions; launching still requires the target app to be whitelisted.
Only these packages can be read or controlled. An empty list allows nothing.
Name a recipe and give it plain JSON tool steps. It runs without any model, only with the tools listed as available. Steps run one at a time and stop on the first failure or approval request.
WorkManager runs it at this interval (15 minutes minimum, may be delayed by battery policy).
Periodic runs must be at least 15 minutes apart.
Automation never approves a tool request on your behalf, and never replays a step whose side effect is unknown.
A previous run was interrupted while it was changing something. Check the device, then confirm before running again. This record survives clearing history.
Back / Home / Recents only work while the current foreground app is whitelisted, so they cannot be used to drive an unauthorized app.

Steps can reuse earlier results: "snapshot_id":"{{0.snapshot_id}}", "node_id":"{{0.nodes.2.id}}" (step index starts at 0). Without such references a recipe only works as a fixed script of independent actions.
Clearing history does not clear a pending side-effect confirmation.
